body:
Triage: **`pm:blocked`**, with the machine half appended to the body (`Blocked-by: #4165`) so the unlock sweep can find it — the body's own sequencing section states "#4165 blocks the whole bump", and #4165 is now a filed `needs-user-decision` card (the `GlobalFilter.defaultValue` refinement vs the `{ preset }` form objectui produces and stores). The other rc.6 red-test items listed here (flow-node schema access strategy, the `sharing_rule` create door, the bare `Invalid input` diagnostics, `ActionSchema.description`) ride behind the same bump, so the card blocks as a unit.

- **Unlock condition**: when #4165 is ruled, this card returns to the queue as a `chore(deps)` bump-and-restore-green of the same shape as #3560 / PR #3568.
- **Dup check**: the bump surface is split deliberately across #4163 (I18nLabel audit + Studio authoring decision), #4164 (widget-manifest prefix reclaim, already `finding`), #4165 (the blocking decision) — cross-referenced from the body; no overlap with any other open card (local filter over cached open lists).
- **Premise**: measurements are from today's resolved rc.5-vs-rc.6 dist diff (40 exports removed / 29 added) filed at 15:13Z — current by construction.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

The parity exemptions: each of the 12 stale entries removed WITH the declaration that obsoletes it verified; the 3 new record-picker inputs declared per the #3830/#4041 worked shape. ⛔ Nothing from #4163/#4164/#4165's territory rides along.

Measured delta from #4223 (an unrelated app-shell card that merged current `main`): **three red surfaces beyond items 1 and 2**, all from the same rc.6 bump. Items 1 and 2 reproduce exactly as this card describes — same symbol list, same key lists — so this is additive, not a re-report.

Measured on `main` merged into a feature branch, `@objectstack/spec` resolving to `17.0.0-rc.6`:

**a. `scripts/__tests__/quick-reference-current-release-4143.test.ts` — 3 failures.** `QUICK_REFERENCE.md`'s "Current Release" block still quotes `^17.0.0-rc.5` for both `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/client`, while the manifests it derives from now declare `^17.0.0-rc.6`:

```
AssertionError: QUICK_REFERENCE.md must state the client range as "^17.0.0-rc.6":
  expected '`@objectstack/client` ^17.0.0-rc.5 (declared by `apps/console/package.json`
  and `packages/data-objectstack/package.json`)' to contain '^17.0.0-rc.6'

AssertionError: QUICK_REFERENCE.md's "Current Release" block states
  ["^17.0.0-rc.5","^17.0.0-rc.5"], which no manifest in this tree produced.
  Derived values are: ["17.4.0","^17.0.0-rc.6","≥22","≥9","10.31.0","18.x","19.x","≥5.0"]
```

Pure documentation follow-through — the test names its own fix.

**b. `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts:123` — 1 failure.** `record:details — the spec really takes OBJECT sections — the id-list spelling is gone, not unioned in`, asserting `expected false to be true`. Same family as item 2 (a registry-vs-spec parity pin), different package, so it is not covered by the `apps/console` carve-out work.

**c. `packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts` — 3 type errors, in the `tsconfig.typetests.json` project.** The widened `I18nLabel` reaches one more site than the eight render sites the card records as repaired:

```
src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts(245,39): error TS2322:
  Type 'ActionParam' is not assignable to type 'RawActionParam'.
    Types of property 'label' are incompatible.
      Type 'string | Record< string, string > | undefined'
        is not assignable to type 'string | undefined'.
```

Also at 345,28 and 358,11. Worth flagging separately because `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.typetests.json` — the **first** command is clean and only the second fails, so a check that stops at `tsc --noEmit` reads green.

## Attribution evidence

Each of these was isolated by reverting the unrelated card's diff to `main` and re-running on the identical tree:

```
with the feature diff:     Tests  6 failed | 60 passed (66)
with the diff removed:     Tests  6 failed | 60 passed (66)   ← identical
```

and the same for the typetests errors (byte-identical output either way). Independently, **`main` itself is red**: the Type Check job failed on `Verify spec-named symbols are derived, not hand-written` at both `38ab5054f` and `a9a67ec5b`, the latter being the base of the PR that measured this.

## Why this is worth a line here

Every PR opened against current `main` inherits all of it, and the shape is confusing: **Lint is green, Type Check is red, and two of four test shards are red** — a mix that reads like the PR's own breakage until the shard logs are opened and every failure turns out to be in a package the PR never touched. Until this card lands, a red Type Check plus red shards 2 and 3 is the expected baseline rather than a signal about the change under review.

Measured from #4211's dispatch (PR #4224), which inherited this red — adding the items **"What is left" does not currently enumerate**, so PR #4189 landing does not leave `main` green by surprise.

Method: `origin/main` @ `a9a67ec5b` checked out **standalone in a detached comparison worktree**, `pnpm install` (resolves `@objectstack/spec@17.0.0-rc.6`), no PR commit present. Every item below reproduces there byte-for-byte identically to the PR branch, so none of it is #4224's.

**Already covered here — confirming, not adding.** Item 1 (`check:spec-symbols`) reproduces; CI reports 8 collisions across `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/types` where this card lists 13, the difference presumably being the `dist` state of the packages the gate reads. Item 2 reproduces with exactly the key list quoted above, both halves.

**Not enumerated above — four test failures and three `tsc` errors.** The `14,609 / 14,615` line records that six cases were knowingly left failing, but only two of the six (the console parity pair, item 2) appear in the worklist. The other four, plus a `tsc` failure that is not a name collision:

1. **`scripts/__tests__/quick-reference-current-release-4143.test.ts` — 2 cases.** `QUICK_REFERENCE.md` still states the client range as `^17.0.0-rc.5` while the manifests now derive `^17.0.0-rc.6`. The test's own message names the fix and the reason it is a test rather than a doc nit:

   ```
   QUICK_REFERENCE.md must state the client range as "^17.0.0-rc.6": expected
   '`@objectstack/client` ^17.0.0-rc.5 (d…' to contain '^17.0.0-rc.6'

   QUICK_REFERENCE.md's "Current Release" block states ["^17.0.0-rc.5","^17.0.0-rc.5"],
   which no manifest in this tree produced. … Derived values are:
   ["17.4.0","^17.0.0-rc.6","≥22","≥9","10.31.0","18.x","19.x","≥5.0"].
   ```

   Purely mechanical, and it is the one item here that any dev can close without a judgment call.

2. **`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity.test.ts` — 2 cases**, at `:123` and `:124` (the `objectForm.data?.sections?.[0]` assertion). Same family as item 2's console parity but a different package, so a fix scoped to `apps/console` will not reach it.

3. **`packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts` — 3 `tsc` errors**, and this one is a *different kind* of item from everything in the worklist — a type-assignability break, not a name collision:

   ```
   src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts(245,39): error TS2322: Type 'ActionParam' is not assignable to type 'RawActionParam'.
   src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts(345,28): error TS2322: …
   src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts(358,11): error TS2322: …
   ```

   It reads as fallout from move 1 in the "Scale of the release" section — `X = z.infer` / `XInput = z.input` becoming `X = z.input` / `XParsed = z.infer` — i.e. a binding that still needs re-pointing **by side**, in a package whose entry in the item-1 collision list (`MetadataState`, `resolveI18nLabel`) would not lead anyone to look here. Worth naming explicitly because it fails the **same `Type Check` job** as `check:spec-symbols`: the gate runs first and exits non-zero, so these three are invisible until the collisions are triaged, and would surface as a "new" red the moment PR #4189 goes green.

Ordering consequence, one line: `Type Check` cannot go green on `check:spec-symbols` alone — item 3 sits behind it in the same job.

No new issue filed: this card plus PR #4189 already own the surface, and a same-hour twin would be objectui#4949-class scatter.

**ACCEPT — train-finisher review of record** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`) — PR #4208, now READY and queued. One squash delivers #4189's content (this card) + #4163 part 1 + the rc.6 residuals, restoring main to green.

Three findings in this delivery deserve the record. (1) The semantic conflict: main's #4222 had extracted `AddressValue` into a new `address-format` module while the train imports the type from `@objectstack/spec/data` — taking main's side alone MOVES the spec-symbols red rather than fixing it (measured: the guard flags the relocated local declaration), so the resolution is a hybrid where the module imports the type from the spec and `AddressField` re-exports THROUGH the module — the relative-path `from` clause being load-bearing for the guard's re-export exemption. (2) The `recordDetailsInputs` diagnosis: the failure was never about `sections` — both fixtures carried `layout: 'custom'`, a key rc.6 rejects by name, and the GREEN fixture was green for a reason unrelated to its assertion (the parse died on `layout` before ever reaching `sections`). Dropped the key, both verdicts back on `sections`, plus a PATH assertion because a bare error code cannot tell the two rejections apart — a vacuous-green made loud. (3) The prediction correction on the reverse verification is stated rather than smoothed (reverting the fixture necessarily removes the new assertion with it).

Measured red set on the combined tree before fixes: spec-symbols RED, typetests GREEN (the train's own content, as designed), quick-reference RED×3, recordDetailsInputs RED×1 — after: ALL GREEN, on a full ladder (build 44/44, type-check 78/78 with typetest receipts, 871 test files / 10524 tests, i18n gates, changesets arbitrated as already-covering). On landing: #4189 closes unmerged (its content rides here — note already posted there), #4231 (main-health tracker) closes, the four held PRs (#4223/#4224/#4226/#4228) get flipped and queued, then the #4165 migration dispatches, then #6955 closes v17.
